newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GF Namibia says Kombat mine still flooding.
newsitem.headline: GF Namibia says Kombat mine still flooding.

text.p: Gold Fields Namibia Ltd said on Thursday that its Kombat copper mine was still flooding and production remained suspended.
Installation of water sealing plugs was proceeding as a matter of urgency, the company said in a statement with fourth quarter results.
The firm first announced the flooding last Friday when it said it expected production to be interrupted for two weeks.
The flooding followed a breakthrough of fissure water on Janaury 7 in a development drive some 300 metres below the surface.
Kombat is one of three mines operated by Gold Fields Namibia subsidiary Tsumeb Corp Ltd which were hit by a crippling three-month strike at affecting both the mines and smelter last year.

Tsumeb said at the time the strike was resolved that it planned to produce around 27,000-28,000 tonnes of blister copper in 1997 and 30,000 tonnes of lead. Production in 1995 was just under 30,000 tonnes of copper and 27,000 tonnes of lead.
Most of the company's lead is produced from bought-in material while copper output is from the three mines.

The company said on Thursday that approximately 1,000 tonnes of copper were produced from toll feed material in December after the strike ended. Lead metal production was from material in the kettles prior to the strike.
A new lead furnace will be commissioned in the current January-March quarter, it added.
Gold Fields Namibia is part of the Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd group.
